findings.evidence: TauCeti/Topology/Path/ExtendIoo.lean:232-234: "the bare-`rfl` elaborator additionally demands that `ofContinuousOnIoo` be `@[expose]`d" → `(rfl)`. TauCeti/Combinatorics/Young/Tableau.lean:119-122 does the same for `Equiv`-valued defs: "deliberately not `@[expose]`d, so the pre-bump `simp [rowFiberEquiv]` has nothing to unfold; the parentheses in `(rfl)` keep the definitional step inside this module". The imported GLn/CosetDecomposition.lean:128-132 and :136-142 also use unexposed defs with `:= (rfl)`.
findings.fix: Drop both `@[expose]`s and parenthesise the four proofs (lines 82, 86, 97, 101) as `(rfl)`, keeping the definitional step inside the module so importers see only the equivalence and its lemmas.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `upperTriEntriesEquiv` (76) and `upperTriEntriesEquivFin` (91) over-exposes both bodies. The stated reason — "the characteristic simp lemmas above cannot be proved without it" — is false: the lemmas are in the same module, where the body is visible regardless; exposure is only demanded by the *bare* `rfl` spelling the author chose.

findings.evidence: GLn/CosetDecomposition.lean:106-108 `unitriMat_apply_lt ... = (B ⟨(i, j), h⟩ : ℕ)` and :162-164 `upperTriGL_apply_lt ... = (a i : ℚ) * (B ⟨(i, j), h⟩ : ℕ)` — anonymous constructor, not `default`. Mathlib/Logic/Unique.lean:110 `theorem eq_default` carries no `@[simp]`, so nothing joins the two normal forms; simp's discrimination key `Inhabited.default` vs `Subtype.mk` never matches.
findings.fix: State both at an arbitrary index pair `q : {ij : Fin 2 × Fin 2 // ij.1 < ij.2}` as ℕ-valued identities (`((upperTriEntriesEquiv a).symm b q : ℕ) = (b : ℕ)`, likewise for the `Fin p` version), which sidesteps the dependent fibre and matches any spelling of `q`; add a corresponding `(B q : ℕ)` form for the forward direction.
findings.issue: `upperTriEntriesEquiv_symm_apply_default` (86) and `upperTriEntriesEquivFin_symm_val` (101) are stated only at the literal argument `default`, so they never fire on `(e.symm b) ⟨(0,1), h⟩` — the spelling produced by `unitriMat_apply_lt` and `upperTriGL_apply_lt`, the only consumers this file exists to feed. `default_indexPair_val` (66) does not bridge them: it is a `.val` equation, and its LHS occurs in the goal only inside the dependent fibre index `Fin (a q.val.2 / a q.val.1)`.

findings.evidence: grep for `!![` under TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing returns only docstring occurrences at this file's lines 19, 48, 90 and GLn/CosetDecomposition.lean:146 (also a docstring), plus an unrelated matrix in GL2/DiagonalCosetDegree.lean:71 — no declaration produces `!![1, b; 0, p]`.
findings.fix: Add the lemma the docstrings promise, e.g. `@[simp] lemma coe_upperTriGL_symm_upperTriEntriesEquivFin (b : Fin p) : (↑(upperTriGL ((upperTriEntriesEquivFin p).symm b)) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℚ) = !![1, b; 0, p]`; otherwise delete the claim from lines 19 and 88-90.
findings.issue: The module docstring (19, 48) and `upperTriEntriesEquivFin`'s docstring (88-90) assert that `upperTriGL` at these entries "runs over the classical `!![1, b; 0, p]`", and the PR calls this "the only adapter the level-`N` Hecke port still needs", but no declaration states it. Transferring AINTLIB's `∑ b ∈ range p, f ∣[k] T_p_upper p _ b` needs the summand identification, not just the index equivalence, so every consumer must re-derive the matrix from `upperTriGL_coe`/`_apply_lt`/`_apply_diag` plus a positivity side condition `∀ i, 0 < ![1, p] i`.

summary: Both defs are `@[expose]`d on a justification the repo's own idiom contradicts, and all four characteristic lemmas use bare `rfl` instead of `(rfl)`, exporting the defeq they exist to replace. The two `symm` lemmas are stated only at the literal `default`, so they cannot fire on the `⟨(0,1), h⟩` spelling every consumer lemma produces, and the advertised `!![1, b; 0, p]` identification has no lemma.
